title: SIU clears Durham cop in fatal shooting of Ajax man
article: The Durham Regional Police officer who fatally shot an Ajax man in December will not be charged.
The Special Investigations Unit has concluded "there are no reasonable grounds" to charge the officer - who remains unnamed - with the shooting death of Michael MacIsaac, 47.
MacIsaac had run naked out of his house the morning of Dec. 2, 2013. Police responded to a call for a man "acting in a strange manner" in the Westney Rd. N. and Williamson Dr. area.

"In the final analysis, the subject officer was in the lawful discharge of his duties when he was confronted by Mr. MacIsaac, armed with a metal table leg approximately one metre in length, who was not complying with commands to stop and drop his weapon," SIU director Tony Loparco said in a release Tuesday evening.

"In the circumstances, the officer's fear for his life seems a reasonable one to have harboured, as was his belief that lethal force was necessary to preserve himself ... I am satisfied the shooting in question was legally justified."
Tonya Littlejohn, MacIsaac's niece, said the family is "devastated" with the decision.

"Our fight is just beginning, we're not just going to go away," she said. "This isn't the last you'll hear from us in any type of action (including legal). We are completely crushed by this decision. My uncle was not a violent man, no matter what picture they try to paint of him - he was not like that.
"To tell us his shooting is nobody's fault is unacceptable."

Littlejohn, 31, said despite immediate family members meeting with the SIU Tuesday night at their lawyer Julian Falconer's Rosedale office, they found out about the decision through the unit's media release.
"We had been sitting here waiting for the results and we read about them on the news release," she said.
However, SIU spokesman Jasbir Brar said the immediate family were notified in person Tuesday "by our lead investigator at the time of the release."
She added the name of the subject officer is only released if he or she is charged.
The SIU alleges MacIsaac picked up a patio table and used it to strike the front door of a neighbourhood house. After the table broke, he was left holding two of its legs.

The subject officer exited his vehicle along with two witness officers, and was making his way to the rear driver's side when he saw MacIsaac approaching him holding one of the metal table legs "in a threatening fashion," according to the SIU's statement.
The officer then drew his firearm, pointed it as MacIsaac and told him to drop his weapon. When MacIsaac kept approaching, the officer fired two shots.
MacIsaac died the next day in hospital.

In a previous interview with the Sun, MacIsaac's family claimed he had run out of the house naked because of a seizure exacerbated by a fever. His wife, Marianne, said he first experienced seizures in his mid-20s, brought on by a childhood head injury that left scar tissue in his brain.
Usually his seizures were "well-controlled" with two types of anti-seizure medication. It was a seizure, not a mental health issue, she insisted.
She insisted MacIsaac ran out of the house holding nothing, "harmless."
"You're hoping they're going to help you contain him or confine him," she said of the police in an interview last month.
In his decision, Loparco wrote that evidence indicated MacIsaac was within a range of about five to seven feet from the officer at the time of the shooting.

The SIU is an arm's length agency of the province that investigates reports involving police where there has been death or serious injury. The role of the director is to consider whether an officer has committed a criminal offence in connection with the incident under investigation, and depending on the evidence, lay a criminal charge or close the file without any charges being laid.
